comments.note: DapperMovieCatalogRepository.GetMovieListAsync now performs two SQL round-trips per call (main aggregate + BatchTagSql). For catalogs with hundreds of thousands of movies, consider caching the batch tag results or using a single query with GROUP_CONCAT to reduce latency. Current two-query approach is correct and simple but worth monitoring as library size grows.

BatchTagSql fetches all movie-tag rows regardless of how many movies are returned by the main query. If GetMovieListAsync is extended with pagination/filtering in a future WP, BatchTagSql should gain a matching WHERE clause to avoid fetching the full movie-tag table on every filtered request.

The count-mismatch defensive guard in GetMovieListAsync returns the unenriched item silently. Since DapperMovieCatalogRepository has no ILogger injected (by design), there is no way to surface this anomaly. If this guard ever fires in production it will be invisible. Consider adding a structured log warning here when a logger is eventually injected, or adding a Serilog static logger as a last resort.

comments.note: Movie-with-no-tags path: storedTagIds.Count=0 matches SQL StoredTagCount=0, count guard passes cleanly, effective set resolves to empty. No issue.

Count-mismatch defensive guard returns unenriched item (EffectiveTagWeight=0, not StoredTagWeight). This is intentional — data inconsistency fallback. Not an AC violation but worth noting the behaviour differs from the IsInitialized=false fallback which does set EffectiveTagWeight=StoredTagWeight.

The count-mismatch defensive guard (DapperMovieCatalogRepository.cs, GetMovieListAsync) has no dedicated test exercising it. A unit test using a mock connection factory that returns mismatched counts would give confidence this guard behaves correctly without a live DB.

Pre-existing CS8765 warnings in tests/VideoIndexer.Tests/TagsManagerTests.cs (lines 344, 372) are unrelated to WP-015 but are surfaced by every full solution build. These could be suppressed with #pragma or fixed to keep the build output clean.

comments.note: A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring: The count-mismatch defensive guard in GetMovieListAsync (DapperMovieCatalogRepository.cs, enrichment loop) silently returns the unenriched MovieListItem with no log output when the batch tag count disagrees with the SQL aggregate StoredTagCount. For a local single-user desktop app this is not an exploitable vulnerability, but any data inconsistency triggering this branch would be invisible. Already documented by the implementation team as a debt item (no ILogger injected by design). Recommendation: add a Warning-level log statement in the mismatch guard branch when a logger is eventually injected.

A03 — Injection: Confirmed zero SQL injection risk. BatchTagSql and MovieListSql are fully static SQL strings. MovieListQuery is an empty sealed record with no user-controlled fields. All other queries use Dapper anonymous-object parameterization throughout (@Hash, @Filename).

No Critical or High security findings identified. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed against the 3 modified source files and 2 manifest docs. New tag enrichment logic (BatchTagSql, effective-set computation) operates entirely on data from trusted local database via parameterized queries and introduces no new attack surface.
